links.comparator_used: General-purpose Gemma 3 4B (4-bit quantized, via Ollama) vs. domain-adapted MedGemma 4B, same prompt, temperature and retrieval setup
links.outcome: Majority-vote accuracy on MedQA-USMLE 4-option test split (1,273 questions, 3 repetitions each)
links.effect: +6.8 pp majority-vote accuracy (53.3% vs. 46.4%, McNemar p < 10^-4)
links.quote: Domain fine-tuning yields a +6.8 percentage-point gain in majority-vote accuracy over the general 4B baseline (53.3% vs. 46.4%, McNemar p < 10^-4).

links.comparator_used: No retrieval (model's weight knowledge alone) vs. retrieved MedMCQA explanation passages inserted into the prompt, in both Gemma 3 4B and MedGemma 4B
links.outcome: Majority-vote accuracy on MedQA-USMLE 4-option test split
links.effect: No statistically significant gain in either model; in the domain-tuned model the point estimate was -1.9 pp (p = 0.16)
links.quote: RAG over MedMCQA explanations does not produce a statistically significant gain in either model, and in the domain-tuned model the point estimate is slightly negative (-1.9 pp, p = 0.16).

design_hint: retrieval grounding added to existing model
